title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last page (88 of 88) of the first draft of an axiomatic 'Analysis situs' (1986). The setting comes from the previous pages. There is a 'contexte' C with a set \mathcal F of 'figures', a least element \emptyset_{\mathcal F}, an order \le, a closure F \mapsto \overline F, and a relation \ll defined by F' \ll F iff F' \le \overline F \lesssim F. There is also a distinguished subset (written \mathcal M or \mathcal U), apparently the irreducible or 'elementary' figures. A 'lieu' is a non-empty figure that is minimal for \ll; these play the role of points or strata. L is the set of lieux. The 'ombre' (shadow) |F| of a figure F is the set of lieux a with a \ll F, so |F| \subset L.

This page defines the 'multiombre' (multi-shadow) of F as the family of subsets \hat F = { |X| : X \in \mathcal M, X \le F } \subset \mathfrak P(L). Here 'X \in F' is shorthand for X \in \mathcal M, X \le F. So |F| \subset L and \hat F \subset \mathfrak P(L).

It then states |F| = \bigcup_{X \in F} |X| = \bigcup_{A \in \hat F} A. Concretely: every lieu a \ll F satisfies a \ll X for some elementary X \le F. This is justified by a proposition on p.78, whose corollary even gives a smallest such X. A marginal note says the proposition below needs only the existence of such an X.

The Proposition: the multiombre \mathfrak P = \hat F of a figure is an 'admissible' family of subsets of L. That is:
(a) for each A \in \mathfrak P, set \delta A = \bigcup_{B \in \mathfrak P, B \subsetneq A} B (the boundary); then \delta A \ne A, i.e. the 'open cell' A^\circ := A \setminus \delta A is non-empty;
(b) for A, B \in \mathfrak P, A \cap B is the union of the members C \in \mathfrak P with C \subset A \cap B.

In modern terms, an admissible family is an abstract 'closed-cell' or stratification datum on a set. It has the following consequences, not stated on this page:
- The open parts A^\circ are pairwise disjoint. If a \in A^\circ \cap B^\circ, (b) gives C \in \mathfrak P with a \in C \subset A \cap B. C \subsetneq A would put a in \delta A, so C = A \subset B; symmetrically B \subset A.
- In the finite (or well-founded) case, the A^\circ partition \bigcup \mathfrak P: take a minimal A containing a; then a \in A^\circ.
- So the pair (\bigcup \mathfrak P, \mathfrak P) is a set stratified by the poset (\mathfrak P, \subset). Each closed cell A is the union of the open cells below it, as for the face poset of a regular cell complex or the strata of a Whitney or tame stratification.

The purpose is to pass from the abstract axiomatics of figures to a combinatorial 'shadow' on the set of lieux. This anticipates a stratified, tame-topological reading of the theory: figures behave like finite unions of closed cells. The page ends with the statement; no proof is given, and the manuscript stops here.
errors: In (a) the union defining \delta A must run over B \in \mathfrak P (members of the family), not over arbitrary proper subsets B of A; otherwise \delta A = A whenever |A| \ge 2. The intended meaning is clear from (b).
The notation alternates between \mathcal M and \mathcal U for the distinguished set of elementary figures, and 'X \in F' abuses notation for X \le F, X \in \mathcal M.
The proposition is stated without proof and the draft ends. The marginal note indicates the author was still deciding which earlier result (existence versus a smallest X) is needed.

Without a finiteness or well-foundedness assumption, the partition of \bigcup \mathfrak P into the A^\circ can fail to be exhaustive; only disjointness follows from (a) and (b) alone. This is not addressed.

ideas.what: Shadow |F| of a figure as a set of minimal 'lieux', and multi-shadow \hat F as the family of shadows of the elementary figures below F, with |F| = \bigcup \hat F
ideas.modern_name: Point-set realization of an abstract lattice of closed sets / spectrum-like construction (points as minimal elements); cell decomposition of a closed set
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone/Wallman-type realizations; in tame topology, van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn (cell decomposition)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is called for programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (1984, §5), but this axiomatics of figures, lieux and ombres does not appear there

ideas.what: Admissible family of subsets: each member has non-empty interior A \ setminus \delta A, and pairwise intersections are unions of members
ideas.modern_name: Abstract (closure-finite) cell complex / poset-stratified set; face-poset condition of regular CW complexes; finite T0 (Alexandrov) space structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937), Tucker, Kovalevsky (abstract cell complexes); stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather)

missed.claim: A 1986 axiomatic, set-free 'analysis situs' (figures, closure, \ll, lieux, shadows, multi-shadows). It aims to recover a stratified cell structure from purely order-theoretic axioms, an abstract framework for the tame topology of Esquisse §5. It was developed independently of, and in parallel with, o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn–Knight 1984–86). This page shows it reaching the point of extracting an 'admissible' (stratification-like) family of subsets from each figure.
missed.quote: La multiombre \mathfrak P = \hat F d'une figure est une famille admissible de parties de L
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own attempted foundations for 'topologie modérée', which are not in the literature. A comparison with o-minimal and other tame-geometric frameworks (e.g. definable stratifications, constructible sheaves on posets) could be of historical and possibly conceptual interest. However, the content on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The proposition itself is elementary combinatorics of cell or stratification families. Its interest lies in documenting an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology project of 1986, whose details are not in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the first inclusion is '|F| \subset L' (the shadow), not '\hat{\hat F} \subset L'. The second is '\hat F \subset \mathfrak P(L)'.
In the union formula the index is 'A \in \hat F' (single hat).
'a \le F', 'a \le X' should read 'a \ll F', 'a \ll X' (double-less-than sign, as in the definition of shadow on p.87).
'X \in \mathcal U' may be '\mathcal M', as on p.87.
The marginal note reads roughly 'Mais pour la proposition, il suffit d'utiliser l'existence [d'un tel X]'.
'(cor. à la prop.)' refers to the proposition cited as on p.78 (reading uncertain).
